# Reference spec — Bookmark management application · Level (A) implementable

- Domain: bookmark management
- Common initial prompt: "I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks."
- Reference OSS: Linkding (Sascha Sieber, https://github.com/sissbruecker/linkding)
  — its public README/docs were **referenced** to derive the feature set; this is
  not a reproduction of a specific product but represents the domain's feature ceiling.
- Spec level: **(A)** — entities, behaviour rules, states, edge cases, and
  acceptance conditions, at a level where a **functionally equivalent
  re-implementation is possible** even if the UI/code differ.
- Status: not a comparison arm but the **coverage upper-bound anchor** and the
  client's standardised tacit knowledge. No execution session.
- Coverage unit: **functional requirement (REF-BM-###)**.

---

## 1. Overview / scope

A single-user application to save, categorise, search, and revisit web links
(bookmarks), and to manage read state and archiving. On save it automatically
collects metadata from the remote page; it organises with tags, search, and
bundles, and preserves a snapshot of the original. The scope below splits into
the user features the client co-constructs (core / extended) and the operational
features excluded from the denominator (infra).

## 2. Core entities

| Entity | Fields | Constraints / relations |
|---|---|---|
| Bookmark | url, title, description, note (markdown), unread flag, archived flag, favicon, preview image, snapshot reference, created-at, updated-at | url required. Many-to-many with tags. Re-saving the same url should lead to editing the existing bookmark, not creating a new one. |
| Tag | name | Name unique within the user scope. Many-to-many with bookmarks. |
| Bundle | name, search term, included tags, excluded tags | A saved filter. When viewed, dynamically selects bookmarks matching the conditions. |
| User settings | default sort, displayed items, font size | Personal profile settings. |

## 3. Functional requirements

### 3.1 Core

- REF-BM-01: Save a bookmark by entering a url.
- REF-BM-02: On save, automatically collect the target page's title, description, favicon, and preview image.
- REF-BM-03: The user can edit the auto-collected title/description before and after saving.
- REF-BM-04: Edit a bookmark's url/title/description/tags/note.
- REF-BM-05: Delete a bookmark.
- REF-BM-06: When re-saving an existing url, guide the user to edit the existing bookmark instead of creating a new one.
- REF-BM-07: Display the bookmark list readability-first, exposing title, description, tags, and favicon per item.
- REF-BM-08: Selecting a list item navigates to the original url.
- REF-BM-09: Assign one or more tags to a bookmark.
- REF-BM-10: On tag entry, offer existing tags as autocomplete.
- REF-BM-11: Select a specific tag to filter to only that tag's bookmarks.
- REF-BM-12: Full-text search over title, description, note, and url.
- REF-BM-13: Search is case-insensitive.
- REF-BM-14: Search tags with the `#tag` syntax.
- REF-BM-15: Use AND/OR/NOT operators and parenthesised groups in the search term (e.g. `rome (#article or #book)`). Rule: the operators themselves must be quoted to be treated as literal search terms.
- REF-BM-16: Search a quoted phrase as an exact match.
- REF-BM-17: Mark a bookmark as "read later" (unread).
- REF-BM-18: View only unread bookmarks separately.
- REF-BM-19: Mark a bookmark as read to remove it from the unread list.
- REF-BM-20: Select multiple bookmarks to perform a bulk action (add/remove tags, read/unread, archive, delete).
- REF-BM-21: Apply a bulk action to the whole collection matching the current filter.
- REF-BM-22: Sort the list by a sort key (date added, title, etc.).

### 3.2 Extended

- REF-BM-23: Write a markdown note on a bookmark and render it when viewing.
- REF-BM-24: Preserve a snapshot of the bookmarked page as local HTML (single file). Rule: if the url is a PDF, download and store the PDF instead of an HTML snapshot.
- REF-BM-25: Support creating a snapshot on the Internet Archive.
- REF-BM-26: Archive a bookmark to hide it from the default list/search while keeping its content.
- REF-BM-27: Distinguish archive from delete — archive is reversible, delete is permanent removal.
- REF-BM-28: View only archived bookmarks as a separate list.
- REF-BM-29: Save a combination of search term and included/excluded tags as a bundle for reuse.
- REF-BM-30: Import bookmarks in Netscape HTML format (preserving title, tags, date added).
- REF-BM-31: Export bookmarks in Netscape HTML format.
- REF-BM-32: Adjust display-related personal settings (default sort, displayed items, font size, etc.).

### 3.3 Infra — excluded from the coverage denominator

- REF-BM-I01: Multi-user support and a self-service admin panel.
- REF-BM-I02: SSO (OIDC) / auth-proxy login.
- REF-BM-I03: Third-party integration REST API.
- REF-BM-I04: Browser extensions (Firefox/Chrome) / bookmarklet / PWA share sheet.
- REF-BM-I05: Backup and raw-data access.

## 4. Edge cases / business rules

- Archived bookmarks are excluded from the default list and ordinary search results, and appear only in the archive list.
- In search, tag search (`#`) and full-text search combine with AND, and boolean/parentheses/phrases are supported.
- "Apply to whole collection" for bulk actions is limited to the scope defined by the current filter (search term / tag / perspective).
- A duplicate save attempt of the same url converges to editing the existing item, preventing duplicates.

1	# Feature Specification: Bookmark Manager
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `001-bookmark-manager`
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-07-13
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "An app to save and manage bookmarks"
10	
11	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
12	
13	### User Story 1 - Save a bookmark (Priority: P1)
14	
15	A user comes across a web page they want to keep. They save it into the app by
16	providing its address, and the app records it — capturing the page's title so it
17	is recognisable later. The saved bookmark appears in their list immediately.
18	
19	**Why this priority**: Saving is the core reason the app exists. Without it,
20	nothing else has value. This alone is a usable product: a place to stash links.
21	
22	**Independent Test**: Add a bookmark by supplying a web address, then confirm it
23	appears in the list with a recognisable title and its address. Delivers the core
24	"keep this link" value on its own.
25	
26	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
27	
28	1. **Given** an empty bookmark list, **When** the user saves a valid web address,
29	   **Then** a new bookmark appears in the list showing its title and address.
30	2. **Given** the user provides an address without a recognisable title source,
31	   **When** they save it, **Then** the bookmark is still saved and the address
32	   itself is shown as the title.
33	3. **Given** the user submits something that is not a valid web address,
34	   **When** they try to save it, **Then** the app rejects it with a clear message
35	   and nothing is added to the list.
36	
37	---
38	
39	### User Story 2 - Browse and open saved bookmarks (Priority: P1)
40	
41	A user opens the app to revisit something they saved. They see their bookmarks in
42	a list, and can open any bookmark's page in their browser with a single action.
43	
44	**Why this priority**: Saved links are worthless if they cannot be retrieved and
45	opened. Together with saving, this forms the minimum viable product.
46	
47	**Independent Test**: With several bookmarks already saved, view the list and
48	activate one, confirming it opens the correct page.
49	
50	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
51	
52	1. **Given** one or more saved bookmarks, **When** the user views the app,
53	   **Then** all bookmarks are listed with title and address.
54	2. **Given** a bookmark in the list, **When** the user activates it, **Then**
55	   its page opens in the browser.
56	3. **Given** an empty list, **When** the user views the app, **Then** a friendly
57	   empty state explains how to add the first bookmark.
58	
59	---
60	
61	### User Story 3 - Organise, search, and edit bookmarks (Priority: P2)
62	
63	As the collection grows, a user needs to find and tidy their bookmarks. They can
64	search by keyword, assign tags, filter by tag, edit a bookmark's details, and
65	delete bookmarks they no longer want.
66	
67	**Why this priority**: Essential once a user has more than a handful of
68	bookmarks, but the app is already useful without it. This is what turns a flat
69	list into a manageable collection.
70	
71	**Independent Test**: With a set of tagged bookmarks, search by a keyword and
72	filter by a tag to confirm only matching bookmarks show; edit one bookmark's
73	title and tags and confirm the change persists; delete one and confirm it is
74	gone.
75	
76	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
77

providing its address, and the app records it — capturing the page's title so it
is recognisable later. The saved bookmark appears in their list immediately.

**Why this priority**: Saving is the core reason the app exists. Without it,

appears in the list with a recognisable title and its address. Delivers the core

   **Then** a new bookmark appears in the list showing its title and address.

   **When** they save it, **Then** the bookmark is still saved and the address
   itself is shown as the title.
3. **Given** the user submits something that is not a valid web address,
   **When** they try to save it, **Then** the app rejects it with a clear message
   and nothing is added to the list.

a list, and can open any bookmark's page in their browser with a single action.

**Why this priority**: Saved links are worthless if they cannot be retrieved and
opened. Together with saving, this forms the minimum viable product.

**Independent Test**: With several bookmarks already saved, view the list and
activate one, confirming it opens the correct page.

Option **A** — single user, on my own device, no logins. It's just me keeping my own links. Good call leaving that open; A is what I want.

Before you treat the rest as approved, though, I went through it carefully and a few things don't quite match what I picture:

1. **When I save a link I already saved** — a warning isn't really what I want. I'd expect it to just take me to the one I already have so I can tweak it (fix the title, add a tag). Not two entries, and not a dead-end "already exists" message.

2. **What gets grabbed automatically** — you've got the title, but in a long list a title alone gets hard to scan. I'd expect it to also pull in the little site icon and a short blurb/description of the page, so each item is recognisable at a glance.

3. **Bringing in my existing bookmarks** — you've put import/export out of scope, and that one I'd push back on. I already have a pile of bookmarks in my browser; being able to bring those in (and get them back out) is honestly a big part of why I'd bother switching to this. I'd really like that in, not later.

4. **Searching** — when I search I'd want to find an exact phrase if I put it in quotes, and to be able to search *within* a tag (e.g. show me things tagged "recipes" that mention "chicken"). And it shouldn't care about capital letters.

5. **Sorting** — "newest first" is a fine default, but sometimes I'd want to flip it to alphabetical by title. I'd like to be able to choose.

6. **Getting things out of the way without losing them** — delete-forever is good to have, but a lot of the time I don't want it gone, I just want it off my main list without throwing it away. Some way to tuck a bookmark aside and still get it back later.

7. **"Read it later"** — I often save things I haven't read yet. I'd love to mark those and be able to look at just my unread pile.

Sort those out and I think we're close. Everything else in the spec reads right to me.

14	
15	A user comes across a web page they want to keep. They save it into the app by
16	providing its address, and the app records it — automatically capturing the
17	page's title, its site icon, and a short description so it is recognisable at a

19	
20	**Why this priority**: Saving is the core reason the app exists. Without it,

22	
23	**Independent Test**: Add a bookmark by supplying a web address, then confirm it
24	appears in the list with a recognisable title, site icon, short description, and
25	its address. Delivers the core "keep this link" value on its own.
26	
27	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
28	
29	1. **Given** an empty bookmark list, **When** the user saves a valid web address,
30	   **Then** a new bookmark appears in the list showing its title, site icon,
31	   short description, and address.
32	2. **Given** the user provides an address whose title cannot be determined,
33	   **When** they save it, **Then** the bookmark is still saved and the address
34	   itself is shown as the title.
35	3. **Given** the user submits something that is not a valid web address,
36	   **When** they try to save it, **Then** the app rejects it with a clear message
37	   and nothing is added to the list.
38	4. **Given** the user saves an address that is already bookmarked, **When** they
39	   submit it, **Then** the app opens the existing bookmark for editing instead of
40	   creating a second entry (see User Story 3).
41	
42	---
43	
44	### User Story 2 - Browse and open saved bookmarks (Priority: P1)
45	
46	A user opens the app to revisit something they saved. They see their bookmarks in
47	a list — each recognisable by its title, site icon, and short description — and
48	can open any bookmark's page in their browser with a single action.
49	
50	**Why this priority**: Saved links are worthless if they cannot be retrieved and
51	opened. Together with saving, this forms the minimum viable product.
52	
53	**Independent Test**: With several bookmarks already saved, view the list and
54	activate one, confirming it opens the correct page.
55	
56	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
57	
58	1. **Given** one or more saved (non-archived) bookmarks, **When** the user views
59	   the app, **Then** all such bookmarks are listed with title, site icon, short
60	   description, and address.
61	2. **Given** a bookmark in the list, **When** the user activates it, **Then**
62	   its page opens in the browser.
63	3. **Given** an empty list, **When** the user views the app, **Then** a friendly
64	   empty state explains how to add the first bookmark.
65	
66	---
67	
68	### User Story 3 - Organise, search, and edit bookmarks (Priority: P2)
69	
70	As the collection grows, a user needs to find and tidy their bookmarks. They can
71	search by keyword (including exact phrases in quotes), assign tags (with
72	suggestions drawn from tags they have already used, so the same tag is not
73	re-created under slightly different spellings), filter by tag, search within a
74	tag, edit a bookmark's details — including notes with light formatting — choose
75	how the list is sorted, and delete bookmarks they no longer want.
76	
77	**Why this priority**: Essential once a user has more than a handful of
78	bookmarks, but the app is already useful without it. This is what turns a flat
79	list into a manageable collection.
80	
81	**Independent Test**: With a set of tagged bookmarks, search by a keyword and by
82	a quoted phrase, filter by a tag and search within it, switch the sort order,
83	edit one bookmark's title and tags and confirm the change persists, and delete
84	one and confirm it is gone.
85	
86	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
87	
88	1. **Given** several bookmarks, **When** the user types a keyword, **Then** the
89	   list narrows to bookmarks whose title, address, description, notes, or tags
90	   match, regardless of letter case.
91	2. **Given** several bookmarks, **When** the user searches for a phrase enclosed
92	   in quotation marks, **Then** only bookmarks containing that exact phrase are
93	   shown.
94	3. **Given** bookmarks with assigned tags, **When** the user selects a tag,
95	   **Then** only bookmarks carrying that tag are shown.
96	4. **Given** a tag filter is active, **When** the user also types a keyword,
97	   **Then** the results are only bookmarks that both carry the tag and match the
98	   keyword (search within a tag).
99	5. **Given** a list of bookmarks, **When** the user chooses a sort order, **Then**
100	   the list reorders accordingly — either most recently saved first (default) or
101	   alphabetically by title.
102	6. **Given** an existing bookmark, **When** the user edits its title, description,
103	   notes, or tags and saves, **Then** the updated details are shown and retained.
104	7. **Given** an existing bookmark, **When** the user deletes it and confirms,
105	   **Then** it is permanently removed and no longer appears in the list or in
106	   searches.
107	8. **Given** the user has previously used one or more tags, **When** they begin
108	   typing a tag, **Then** matching existing tags are suggested for selection so
109	   they can reuse an existing tag rather than create a near-duplicate.
110	9. **Given** the user writes a note with light formatting (such as bold text, a
111	   list, or a link), **When** they view the bookmark, **Then** the note is
112	   displayed with that formatting laid out, not as a single plain-text blob.
113	
114	---
115	
116	### User Story 4 - Import and export bookmarks (Priority: P2)
117	
118	A user already has a pile of bookmarks in their web browser and wants to bring
119	them into the app, and to be able to take their whole collection back out again
120	later. They import from a standard browser bookmark file, and can export their
121	collection to a file at any time.
122	
123	**Why this priority**: A primary reason for adopting the app is consolidating
124	bookmarks the user already has; being able to export again means their data is
125	never trapped. Not part of the bare MVP, but a key adoption driver the user
126	wants available, not deferred.
127	
128	**Independent Test**: Import a standard browser bookmark export file and confirm
129	the bookmarks appear in the list with their titles, addresses, and any folder
130	labels; then export the collection and confirm the resulting file contains all
131	of them.
132	
133	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
134	
135	1. **Given** a standard browser bookmark export file, **When** the user imports
136	   it, **Then** each bookmark in the file is added to the collection with its
137	   title and address.
138	2. **Given** an import file whose bookmarks are organised into folders, **When**
139	   the user imports it, **Then** each bookmark's containing folder name(s) are
140	   brought across as tags so the original organisation is preserved.
141	3. **Given** an import file that records when each bookmark was originally added,
142	   **When** the user imports it, **Then** the original "date added" is kept rather
143	   than reset to the import date.
144	4. **Given** an import file that includes an address the user has already saved,
145	   **When** the user imports it, **Then** no duplicate entry is created for that
146	   address.
147	5. **Given** a collection of saved bookmarks, **When** the user exports, **Then**
148	   a file is produced that contains all of their bookmarks and can be re-imported
149	   into the app or into a standard web browser.
150	
151	---
152	
153	### User Story 5 - Triage: read-later and archive (Priority: P2)
154	
155	A user often saves things they have not read yet and wants to see just that
156	unread pile. They also want to clear finished or low-priority items off their
157	main list without throwing them away — tucking them aside and retrieving them
158	later if needed.
159	
160	**Why this priority**: Keeps the main list focused and supports the common
161	"save now, read later" habit. Valuable for daily use, but the app still works
162	without it.
163

165	unread pile; archive a bookmark, confirm it leaves the main list, then find it in

170	1. **Given** a bookmark, **When** the user marks it as unread (read-later),
171	   **Then** it appears when the user filters to their unread pile.
172	2. **Given** a bookmark marked unread, **When** the user marks it as read,
173	   **Then** it no longer appears in the unread pile.
174	3. **Given** a bookmark on the main list, **When** the user archives it, **Then**
175	   it is removed from the main list but retained in the archive.
176	4. **Given** an archived bookmark, **When** the user views the archive and
177	   restores it, **Then** it reappears on the main list unchanged.
178	
179	---
180	
181	### User Story 6 - Act on many bookmarks at once (Priority: P2)
182	
183	A user — most often right after importing a large batch — wants to tidy many
184	bookmarks together instead of one at a time. They select multiple bookmarks and
185	apply a single action to all of them: add a tag, archive, mark read/unread, or
186	delete.
187	
188	**Why this priority**: Without bulk actions, tidying an imported pile of a
189	thousand bookmarks one by one is impractical, undermining the value of import.
190	The app still functions without it, so it sits alongside the other P2
191	enhancements rather than in the MVP.
192	
193	**Independent Test**: Select several bookmarks, apply a tag to all of them in one
194	action, and confirm every selected bookmark now carries that tag; repeat for
195	archive, mark-read, and delete.
196	
197	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
198	
199	1. **Given** several bookmarks, **When** the user selects multiple and applies a
200	   tag, **Then** every selected bookmark receives that tag.
201	2. **Given** several selected bookmarks, **When** the user archives the
202	   selection, **Then** all of them are archived in one action.
203	3. **Given** several selected bookmarks, **When** the user marks the selection as
204	   read or unread, **Then** all of them change to that status together.
205	4. **Given** several selected bookmarks, **When** the user deletes the selection
206	   and confirms, **Then** all of them are permanently removed in one action.
207	
208	---
209	
210	### User Story 7 - Save a frequently used search (Priority: P3)
211	
212	A user who repeatedly applies the same combination of keyword and tag filters
213	(for example, "unread cooking articles") wants to save that combination and
214	return to it in one step, without setting it up each time.
215	
216	**Why this priority**: A convenience layered on top of search and filtering; it
217	adds no new data and the app is fully usable without it. Nice-to-have, and
218	acceptable to defer if it proves costly.
219	
220	**Independent Test**: Set up a search combining a keyword, a tag, and the unread
221	filter; save it under a name; clear everything; then reopen the saved search and
222	confirm the same results return.
223	
224	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
225	
226	1. **Given** an active combination of keyword and/or tag and/or unread filters,
227	   **When** the user saves it under a name, **Then** it is stored and listed as a
228	   named saved search.
229	2. **Given** a named saved search, **When** the user opens it, **Then** the app
230	   applies that combination of filters and shows the matching bookmarks.
231	
232	---
233	
234	### Edge Cases
235	
236	- **Re-saving an existing address**: The app does not create a duplicate; instead
237	  it opens the already-saved bookmark so the user can adjust it (fix the title,
238	  add a tag, etc.).
239	- **Unreachable page on save**: If the title, site icon, or description cannot be
240	  retrieved (site offline, blocked, or slow), the bookmark is still saved using
241	  the address as its title and whatever metadata is available; saving never
242	  blocks on the remote page.
243	- **Import containing duplicates**: Addresses already in the collection are not
244	  added again as duplicates during import.
245	- **Very long titles, descriptions, or addresses**: The list display truncates
246	  gracefully without breaking layout; the full value remains available.
247	- **Deleting a tag in use**: Removing a tag from a bookmark does not delete other
248	  bookmarks; a tag with no remaining bookmarks simply disappears from the filter
249	  list.
250	- **Search with no matches**: A clear "no results" state is shown, with an easy
251	  way to clear the search.
252	- **Archived items in search**: Archived bookmarks do not appear in the main list
253	  or default search; they are found via the archive view.
254	- **Nested import folders**: Bookmarks nested several folders deep are still
255	  imported; each folder level in the path is available as a tag.
256	- **Bulk delete**: A bulk delete still requires a single confirmation before the
257	  selected bookmarks are permanently removed.
258	
259	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
260	
261	### Functional Requirements
262	
263	- **FR-001**: System MUST allow a user to save a bookmark by providing a web
264	  address.
265	- **FR-002**: System MUST validate that the supplied address is a well-formed web
266	  address and reject malformed input with a clear message.
267	- **FR-003**: System MUST automatically capture, on a best-effort basis, the
268	  page's title, its site icon, and a short description for each saved bookmark,
269	  falling back to the address as the title when a title cannot be determined.
270	- **FR-004**: System MUST let the user optionally add or override the title, add
271	  notes, add a description, and assign one or more tags when saving or editing a
272	  bookmark.
273	- **FR-004a**: When the user assigns a tag, the system MUST suggest tags the user
274	  has already used that match what is being typed, so existing tags can be reused
275	  instead of near-duplicates being created.
276	- **FR-004b**: System MUST let users apply light formatting to notes (at minimum
277	  bold text, lists, and links) and MUST display notes with that formatting laid
278	  out rather than as plain text.
279	- **FR-005**: System MUST display saved bookmarks in a list showing at least the
280	  title, site icon, short description, and address.
281	- **FR-006**: Users MUST be able to open a bookmark's page in their web browser
282	  from the list.
283	- **FR-007**: Users MUST be able to edit an existing bookmark's title,
284	  description, notes, and tags.
285	- **FR-008**: Users MUST be able to permanently delete a bookmark, with a
286	  confirmation step to prevent accidental loss.
287	- **FR-009**: System MUST let users search bookmarks by keyword, matching against
288	  title, address, description, notes, and tags; search MUST ignore letter case
289	  and MUST treat a quoted phrase as an exact-phrase match.
290	- **FR-010**: System MUST let users filter bookmarks by tag, and MUST allow a
291	  keyword search to be combined with an active tag filter (search within a tag).
292	- **FR-011**: When a user attempts to save an address that is already bookmarked,
293	  the system MUST open the existing bookmark for editing instead of creating a
294	  duplicate entry.
295	- **FR-012**: System MUST persist bookmarks locally on the user's own device so
296	  they remain available across app restarts, for a single user with no accounts
297	  or login.
298	- **FR-013**: System MUST record when each bookmark was saved and let the user
299	  choose the list order, defaulting to most recently saved first and offering
300	  alphabetical-by-title as an alternative.
301	- **FR-014**: System MUST let users import bookmarks from a standard browser
302	  bookmark export file, adding each imported bookmark to the collection without
303	  creating duplicates of addresses already saved. During import the system MUST
304	  convert each bookmark's containing folder name(s) into tags, and MUST preserve
305	  the original "date added" recorded in the file rather than resetting it to the
306	  import date.
307	- **FR-015**: System MUST let users export their entire bookmark collection to a
308	  file that can be re-imported into the app or into a standard web browser.
309	- **FR-016**: System MUST let users archive a bookmark (removing it from the main
310	  list while retaining it) and later restore an archived bookmark to the main
311	  list; archived bookmarks are excluded from the main list and default search.
312	- **FR-017**: System MUST let users mark a bookmark as read or unread and filter
313	  the collection to show only unread ("read later") bookmarks.
314	- **FR-018**: System MUST let users select multiple bookmarks and apply a single
315	  action to all of them at once — at minimum: add a tag, archive, mark
316	  read/unread, and delete (deletion still requiring confirmation).
317	- **FR-019**: System SHOULD let users save a named combination of keyword and/or
318	  tag and/or unread filters as a saved search and reapply it in one step. (Lower
319	  priority; may be deferred if implementation proves costly.)
320	
321	### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*
322	
323	- **Bookmark**: A saved link. Key attributes: web address, title, site icon,
324	  short description, optional user notes (with light formatting), set of tags,
325	  date added (preserved from import where available, otherwise the save date),
326	  read/unread status, archived state. Belongs to the user's single local
327	  collection.
328	- **Tag**: A short user-defined label used to group and filter bookmarks, reused
329	  across bookmarks via suggestions to avoid near-duplicates. A bookmark may have
330	  many tags; a tag may apply to many bookmarks. Import folder names become tags.
331	- **Saved Search**: A named, reusable combination of keyword and/or tag and/or
332	  unread filters that the user can reapply in one step. (Associated with the
333	  lower-priority FR-019.)
334	
335	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
336	
337	### Measurable Outcomes
338	
339	- **SC-001**: A user can save a new bookmark in under 15 seconds from opening the
340	  app to seeing it in the list.
341	- **SC-002**: A user can locate a specific bookmark in a collection of 500 in
342	  under 10 seconds using search or tag filtering.
343	- **SC-003**: 95% of saved bookmarks display a meaningful title and site icon
344	  (derived from the page rather than just the raw address).
345	- **SC-004**: Opening a saved bookmark launches the correct page on the first
346	  attempt in 99% of cases.
347	- **SC-005**: No user action results in accidental permanent loss of a bookmark
348	  without a confirmation step; archived bookmarks are 100% recoverable.
349	- **SC-006**: Saved bookmarks are still present after closing and reopening the
350	  app 100% of the time.
351	- **SC-007**: Importing a browser bookmark file of 1,000 bookmarks completes and
352	  makes them all searchable, with folder names carried over as tags, original
353	  dates preserved, and no duplicate entries for addresses already saved.
354	- **SC-009**: A user can apply a single action (tag, archive, mark read/unread,
355	  or delete) to 100 selected bookmarks in one operation.
356	- **SC-008**: A user can export their collection and successfully re-import the
357	  resulting file with no loss of bookmarks.
358	
359	## Assumptions
360	
361	- The app manages web-page bookmarks (http/https addresses); other link types
362	  (files, email addresses) are out of scope for v1.
363	- A single person uses the app on their own device to manage their own personal
364	  collection; there are no user accounts, logins, or cross-device sync in v1, and
365	  sharing collections between people is out of scope.
366	- Automatic capture of title, site icon, and description is best-effort; the app
367	  never blocks saving on retrieving remote page metadata.
368	- Import and export use a standard, widely-supported browser bookmark file format
369	  so bookmarks can move between this app and common web browsers.
370	- The app is used on a device with a web browser available to open links.

### User Story 4 - Import and export bookmarks (Priority: P2)

A user already has a pile of bookmarks in their web browser and wants to bring
them into the app, and to be able to take their whole collection back out again
later. They import from a standard browser bookmark file, and can export their
collection to a file at any time.

**Why this priority**: A primary reason for adopting the app is consolidating
bookmarks the user already has; being able to export again means their data is
never trapped. Not part of the bare MVP, but a key adoption driver the user
wants available, not deferred.

**Independent Test**: Import a standard browser bookmark export file and confirm
the bookmarks appear in the list with their titles, addresses, and any folder
labels; then export the collection and confirm the resulting file contains all
of them.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a standard browser bookmark export file, **When** the user imports
   it, **Then** each bookmark in the file is added to the collection with its
   title and address.
2. **Given** an import file whose bookmarks are organised into folders, **When**
   the user imports it, **Then** each bookmark's containing folder name(s) are
   brought across as tags so the original organisation is preserved.
3. **Given** an import file that records when each bookmark was originally added,
   **When** the user imports it, **Then** the original "date added" is kept rather
   than reset to the import date.
4. **Given** an import file that includes an address the user has already saved,
   **When** the user imports it, **Then** no duplicate entry is created for that
   address.
5. **Given** a collection of saved bookmarks, **When** the user exports, **Then**
   a file is produced that contains all of their bookmarks and can be re-imported
   into the app or into a standard web browser.

---

### User Story 5 - Triage: read-later and archive (Priority: P2)

A user often saves things they have not read yet and wants to see just that
unread pile. They also want to clear finished or low-priority items off their
main list without throwing them away — tucking them aside and retrieving them
later if needed.

**Why this priority**: Keeps the main list focused and supports the common
"save now, read later" habit. Valuable for daily use, but the app still works
without it.

**Independent Test**: Mark some bookmarks unread and filter to show only the
unread pile; archive a bookmark, confirm it leaves the main list, then find it in
the archive and restore it to the main list.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a bookmark, **When** the user marks it as unread (read-later),
   **Then** it appears when the user filters to their unread pile.
2. **Given** a bookmark marked unread, **When** the user marks it as read,
   **Then** it no longer appears in the unread pile.
3. **Given** a bookmark on the main list, **When** the user archives it, **Then**
   it is removed from the main list but retained in the archive.
4. **Given** an archived bookmark, **When** the user views the archive and
   restores it, **Then** it reappears on the main list unchanged.

---

### User Story 6 - Act on many bookmarks at once (Priority: P2)

A user — most often right after importing a large batch — wants to tidy many
bookmarks together instead of one at a time. They select multiple bookmarks and
apply a single action to all of them: add a tag, archive, mark read/unread, or
delete.

**Why this priority**: Without bulk actions, tidying an imported pile of a
thousand bookmarks one by one is impractical, undermining the value of import.
The app still functions without it, so it sits alongside the other P2
enhancements rather than in the MVP.

**Independent Test**: Select several bookmarks, apply a tag to all of them in one
action, and confirm every selected bookmark now carries that tag; repeat for
archive, mark-read, and delete.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** several bookmarks, **When** the user selects multiple and applies a
   tag, **Then** every selected bookmark receives that tag.
2. **Given** several selected bookmarks, **When** the user archives the
   selection, **Then** all of them are archived in one action.
3. **Given** several selected bookmarks, **When** the user marks the selection as
   read or unread, **Then** all of them change to that status together.
4. **Given** several selected bookmarks, **When** the user deletes the selection
   and confirms, **Then** all of them are permanently removed in one action.

---

### User Story 7 - Save a frequently used search (Priority: P3)

A user who repeatedly applies the same combination of keyword and tag filters
(for example, "unread cooking articles") wants to save that combination and
return to it in one step, without setting it up each time.

**Why this priority**: A convenience layered on top of search and filtering; it
adds no new data and the app is fully usable without it. Nice-to-have, and
acceptable to defer if it proves costly.

**Independent Test**: Set up a search combining a keyword, a tag, and the unread
filter; save it under a name; clear everything; then reopen the saved search and
confirm the same results return.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an active combination of keyword and/or tag and/or unread filters,
   **When** the user saves it under a name, **Then** it is stored and listed as a
   named saved search.
2. **Given** a named saved search, **When** the user opens it, **Then** the app
   applies that combination of filters and shows the matching bookmarks.

### Edge Cases

- **Re-saving an existing address**: The app does not create a duplicate; instead
  it opens the already-saved bookmark so the user can adjust it (fix the title,
  add a tag, etc.).
- **Unreachable page on save**: If the title, site icon, or description cannot be
  retrieved (site offline, blocked, or slow), the bookmark is still saved using
  the address as its title and whatever metadata is available; saving never
  blocks on the remote page.
- **Import containing duplicates**: Addresses already in the collection are not
  added again as duplicates during import.
- **Very long titles, descriptions, or addresses**: The list display truncates
  gracefully without breaking layout; the full value remains available.
- **Deleting a tag in use**: Removing a tag from a bookmark does not delete other
  bookmarks; a tag with no remaining bookmarks simply disappears from the filter
  list.
- **Search with no matches**: A clear "no results" state is shown, with an easy
  way to clear the search.
- **Archived items in search**: Archived bookmarks do not appear in the main list
  or default search; they are found via the archive view.
- **Nested import folders**: Bookmarks nested several folders deep are still
  imported; each folder level in the path is available as a tag.
- **Bulk delete**: A bulk delete still requires a single confirmation before the
  selected bookmarks are permanently removed.

  address.

  address and reject malformed input with a clear message.
- **FR-003**: System MUST automatically capture, on a best-effort basis, the
  page's title, its site icon, and a short description for each saved bookmark,
  falling back to the address as the title when a title cannot be determined.

  notes, add a description, and assign one or more tags when saving or editing a
  bookmark.

  has already used that match what is being typed, so existing tags can be reused
  instead of near-duplicates being created.
- **FR-004b**: System MUST let users apply light formatting to notes (at minimum
  bold text, lists, and links) and MUST display notes with that formatting laid
  out rather than as plain text.
- **FR-005**: System MUST display saved bookmarks in a list showing at least the
  title, site icon, short description, and address.
- **FR-006**: Users MUST be able to open a bookmark's page in their web browser

- **FR-007**: Users MUST be able to edit an existing bookmark's title,
  description, notes, and tags.
- **FR-008**: Users MUST be able to permanently delete a bookmark, with a
  confirmation step to prevent accidental loss.
- **FR-009**: System MUST let users search bookmarks by keyword, matching against
  title, address, description, notes, and tags; search MUST ignore letter case
  and MUST treat a quoted phrase as an exact-phrase match.
- **FR-010**: System MUST let users filter bookmarks by tag, and MUST allow a
  keyword search to be combined with an active tag filter (search within a tag).
- **FR-011**: When a user attempts to save an address that is already bookmarked,
  the system MUST open the existing bookmark for editing instead of creating a
  duplicate entry.

  they remain available across app restarts, for a single user with no accounts
  or login.

  choose the list order, defaulting to most recently saved first and offering
  alphabetical-by-title as an alternative.

  creating duplicates of addresses already saved. During import the system MUST
  convert each bookmark's containing folder name(s) into tags, and MUST preserve
  the original "date added" recorded in the file rather than resetting it to the
  import date.
- **FR-015**: System MUST let users export their entire bookmark collection to a
  file that can be re-imported into the app or into a standard web browser.
- **FR-016**: System MUST let users archive a bookmark (removing it from the main
  list while retaining it) and later restore an archived bookmark to the main
  list; archived bookmarks are excluded from the main list and default search.
- **FR-017**: System MUST let users mark a bookmark as read or unread and filter
  the collection to show only unread ("read later") bookmarks.
- **FR-018**: System MUST let users select multiple bookmarks and apply a single
  action to all of them at once — at minimum: add a tag, archive, mark
  read/unread, and delete (deletion still requiring confirmation).
- **FR-019**: System SHOULD let users save a named combination of keyword and/or
  tag and/or unread filters as a saved search and reapply it in one step. (Lower
  priority; may be deferred if implementation proves costly.)

### Key Entities *(include if feature involves data)*

- **Bookmark**: A saved link. Key attributes: web address, title, site icon,
  short description, optional user notes (with light formatting), set of tags,
  date added (preserved from import where available, otherwise the save date),
  read/unread status, archived state. Belongs to the user's single local
  collection.
- **Tag**: A short user-defined label used to group and filter bookmarks, reused
  across bookmarks via suggestions to avoid near-duplicates. A bookmark may have
  many tags; a tag may apply to many bookmarks. Import folder names become tags.
- **Saved Search**: A named, reusable combination of keyword and/or tag and/or
  unread filters that the user can reapply in one step. (Associated with the
  lower-priority FR-019.)

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: A user can save a new bookmark in under 15 seconds from opening the
  app to seeing it in the list.
- **SC-002**: A user can locate a specific bookmark in a collection of 500 in
  under 10 seconds using search or tag filtering.
- **SC-003**: 95% of saved bookmarks display a meaningful title and site icon
  (derived from the page rather than just the raw address).
- **SC-004**: Opening a saved bookmark launches the correct page on the first
  attempt in 99% of cases.
- **SC-005**: No user action results in accidental permanent loss of a bookmark
  without a confirmation step; archived bookmarks are 100% recoverable.
- **SC-006**: Saved bookmarks are still present after closing and reopening the
  app 100% of the time.
- **SC-007**: Importing a browser bookmark file of 1,000 bookmarks completes and

  dates preserved, and no duplicate entries for addresses already saved.
- **SC-009**: A user can apply a single action (tag, archive, mark read/unread,
  or delete) to 100 selected bookmarks in one operation.
- **SC-008**: A user can export their collection and successfully re-import the
  resulting file with no loss of bookmarks.

- The app manages web-page bookmarks (http/https addresses); other link types
  (files, email addresses) are out of scope for v1.
- A single person uses the app on their own device to manage their own personal
  collection; there are no user accounts, logins, or cross-device sync in v1, and
  sharing collections between people is out of scope.
- Automatic capture of title, site icon, and description is best-effort; the app
  never blocks saving on retrieving remote page metadata.
- Import and export use a standard, widely-supported browser bookmark file format
  so bookmarks can move between this app and common web browsers.
- The app is used on a device with a web browser available to open links.
